> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.
# Noul
> A Noul question asks the TypeSafe model to evaluate a yes/no question and return the probability that the answer is yes.
Use a Noul when the answer is yes or no. For example, does this message ask for a refund, does this resume mention distributed systems, does this comment contain personal data. If the answer is one of several options, use a [Choice](/primitives/choice). If it's a position on a spectrum, use a [Score](/primitives/score). [Choose a question type](/primitives#choose-a-question-type) compares all three.
A Noul answer is a single number representing the probability that the answer is yes where 0 means no and 1 means yes.
## Request structure
The POST request body to the [TypeSafe API](/api) has the same three top-level fields as any other question type: `state`, which is the content to evaluate; `model`; and `questions`. Each Noul question has the following fields:
* `type`: Always `"noul"`.
* `instructions`: The yes/no question the model answers, or a statement for it to judge.
* `criteria`: Optional. An object with `true` and `false` descriptions of what a yes and a no mean.
Below is a request where the state is a support message and the two questions are whether the customer wants a person and whether they have contacted support before:
Try it in the Playground →
You choose the question ids, `is_human_escalation` and `is_repeat_contact` here. The ids are not sent to the model. Each answer is returned under the same id. The first question relies on `instructions` alone. The second adds `criteria` to say what counts as a yes and what counts as a no.
With the [Python SDK](/sdk/python), the same questions are `Noul` objects:
```python theme={null}
from typesafe_sdk import Noul, NoulCriteria, TypeSafeClient
with TypeSafeClient() as client:
    response = client.system_one(
        model="jev-latest",
        state="I have asked three times now. Can I please just talk to a real person?",
        questions={
            "is_human_escalation": Noul(
                instructions="Is the customer asking for a human agent?",
            ),
            "is_repeat_contact": Noul(
                instructions="Has the customer contacted support about this before?",
                criteria=NoulCriteria(
                    true="Mentions a prior attempt, ticket, or that they have asked before",
                    false="No sign of any previous contact",
                ),
            ),
        },
    )
    print(response.answers["is_human_escalation"].noul)
    print(response.answers["is_repeat_contact"].noul)
```
The `system_one` method and the `https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone` endpoint are both named after [System One](/concepts/system-one), TypeSafe's AI model. [How to build with TypeSafe](/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one) covers where to use it in your code.
If you're using a coding agent, install the [TypeSafe agent skill](/agent-skill#installation) first so it knows the request and response shapes.
> [!NOTE]
>
> `instructions` can be a string, an object, or an array. Start with a string. Use an object when the question needs data alongside it, such as a record to compare the state against, or when part of the question is built by your code. [Use structure in the questions](/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one#use-structure-in-the-questions) explains when structure helps, and [the example below](#structured-instructions) shows it with questions built in code.
## Response structure
The response has one entry in `answers` per question, under the ids from the request:
```json theme={null}
{
  "model": "jev-1.13.0",
  "answers": {
    "is_human_escalation": {
      "type": "noul",
      "noul": 0.99
    },
    "is_repeat_contact": {
      "type": "noul",
      "noul": 0.93
    }
  },
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 360,
    "output_tokens": 39
  }
}
```
Both answers here are close to 1. The customer says "talk to a real person", so `is_human_escalation` is 0.99. "I have asked three times now" matches the `true` description of `is_repeat_contact`, so it is 0.93.
## Reading a Noul
The number is the answer and the certainty in one. A value near 1 is a strong yes. A value near 0 is a strong no. A value near 0.5 means the model gives yes and no similar probability.
The table below shows recorded `jev-1.13.0` answers to the `is_human_escalation` question for different customer messages:
| State | `noul` |
| - | - |
| Thanks, that fixed it! | 0.02 |
| How do I reset my password? | 0.07 |
| I need this sorted today, whatever it takes. | 0.26 |
| Are you a bot? | 0.40 |
| Is there any way to speak to someone about my invoice? | 0.84 |
| I have asked three times now. Can I please just talk to a real person? | 0.99 |
The first two and the last two are clear. "I need this sorted today" is urgent but never asks for a person, and gets 0.26. "Are you a bot?" hints at wanting a human without asking for one, and the model splits almost evenly at 0.40. Both are the kind of message where a decision needs to be made based on a threshold in your code.
There is no separate `confidence` value for a Noul, unlike a [Choice](/primitives/choice) or a [Score](/primitives/score). A Noul's probability distribution has only two outcomes, yes and no, so the single `noul` value describes it completely. A Choice or Score spreads probability over several options or levels, and `confidence` summarizes that spread.
Most often your code thresholds `noul` into a boolean:
```python theme={null}
wants_human = response.answers["is_human_escalation"].noul > 0.9
if wants_human:
    route_to_agent(ticket)
else:
    route_to_bot(ticket)
```
Where to set the threshold depends on the cost of being wrong. Use 0.5 when yes and no are equally easy to act on. Raise it when acting on a false yes is expensive, such as paging someone or issuing a refund. Lower it when missing a true yes is expensive, such as failing to flag a safety issue. Values in the middle can go to a person rather than either code path. That is the same three-way split the [Confidence](/confidence#three-paths-for-using-confidence-in-your-code) page describes for Choice and Score answers.
A Noul value runs from 0 to 1, but it's not a scale of the thing you asked about. It is the probability that the answer is yes. If the question is really about degree, the value does not measure the degree. Below, "Is the candidate strong in Python?" is asked about four candidates, next to a [Score](/primitives/score) with four levels: no experience, some familiarity, regular use in a job, deep expertise.
| Candidate | Noul: "Is the candidate strong in Python?" | Score: "How much Python experience does the candidate have?" |
| - | - | - |
| My experience is in Java and Go. I have not used Python. | 0.03 | 0.0 (No experience) |
| I have used Python occasionally for small scripts alongside my main Java work. | 0.14 | 1.0 (Some familiarity) |
| I used Python every day for two years in my last job, mostly data pipelines. | 0.81 | 2.05 (Regular use in a job) |
| I have written Python daily for eight years, including maintaining a large Django codebase. | 0.92 | 2.89 (Deep expertise) |
The Noul judges one proposition, "strong", and the values are how likely it is. You could create levels in the 0 to 1 range in your code, such as 0.3 to 0.7 for "some experience", but the model will not see them, so nothing in the answer was judged against them. A middle value can mean medium experience or an unclear case, and the spacing between candidates is not something you chose. The Score judges each level description on its own, so every candidate landed on or near a level you wrote, and the returned probabilities show how the model divided its judgment between levels. If you disagree, reword a level and run it again. [Choose a question type](/primitives#choose-a-question-type) explains the distinction.
## Writing a Noul question
Ask one yes/no question per Noul. If a question has two conditions, such as "Is the customer angry and asking for a refund?", the model has to judge both at once and the value means less. Ask two Nouls and combine them in code.
Phrase the question so that a high value means yes. "Does the message contain personal data?" is clear. "Is the message free of personal data?" inverts the meaning, and code that reads it later will get it backwards.
A statement works as well as a question. For "The customer is requesting a refund", a value near 1 means the statement is true. Try both phrasings with your own data to see which works better.
Make the boundary between yes and no unambiguous. "Does this candidate have any Python experience?" works well because "any" leaves no middle ground. When the boundary is subtle, add `criteria` with `true` and `false` descriptions, as the `is_repeat_contact` question above does. The instruction is enough for most Nouls, so try your questions with and without `criteria` and keep whichever gives better answers on your documents.
## Good practice: ask more than one question per call
For a checklist of conditions, ask many Noul questions in one request: one question per condition, and the code decides what the combination means. Questions are evaluated in parallel, so adding Nouls barely changes the response time. [Ask multiple questions together](/primitives#ask-multiple-questions-together) explains this in more detail.
## Handling multiple Noul answers in code
The two-question request above gives the code enough to route the message. The example below escalates to a person when the customer asks for one, and raises the priority when they have been in touch before. A value in the middle on either question goes to a reviewer instead of a code path:
```python theme={null}
from typesafe_sdk import Noul, NoulCriteria, TypeSafeClient
SUPPORT_QUESTIONS = {
    "is_human_escalation": Noul(
        instructions="Is the customer asking for a human agent?",
    ),
    "is_repeat_contact": Noul(
        instructions="Has the customer contacted support about this before?",
        criteria=NoulCriteria(
            true="Mentions a prior attempt, ticket, or that they have asked before",
            false="No sign of any previous contact",
        ),
    ),
}

NO = 0.2

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build Eric's blind answer-key audit sheet (DRIVE_TRIAGE_PREREG.md, answer-key audit).

    python drive_triage/make_audit.py

Takes every file where Jev clears the 0.50 cut and its domain differs from the answer key,
draws a random 20 (seed 20260928) if there are more, shuffles them and hides which side
is which. Writes private/audit_sheet.md (input and the two answers only; Eric fills in
A, B or neither) and private/audit_key.json (the unblinding map). Both are gitignored:
the sheet carries first-page text, and the map must not be seen before Eric judges.
"""
import csv
import json
import random
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent / "zotero_classify"))
import taxonomy  # noqa: E402

SEED, CUT, MAX = 20260928, 0.50, 20


def main() -> None:
    key = {r["sample_id"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(open(HERE / "answer_key.csv", encoding="utf-8"))}
    jev = [json.loads(l) for l in open(HERE / "runs" / "jev.jsonl", encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
    state = {json.loads(l)["sample_id"]: json.loads(l)["state"]
             for l in open(HERE / "private" / "state.jsonl", encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()}
    dis = sorted((r for r in jev if r["confidence"] >= CUT and r["domain"] != key[r["sample_id"]]["domain"]),
                 key=lambda r: r["sample_id"])
    rng = random.Random(SEED)
    pick = rng.sample(dis, MAX) if len(dis) > MAX else dis
    rng.shuffle(pick)
    lines = ["# Drive triage audit (blind)", "",
             f"{len(pick)} files (of {len(dis)} disagreements). For each, two answers give the file's "
             "domain (and topic). Pick the one that fits the file better from what you see: "
             "write A, B, or N (neither) on the Verdict line. Judge only from the input shown.", ""]
    unblind = {}
    for i, r in enumerate(pick, 1):
        k = key[r["sample_id"]]
        sides = [("jev", r["domain"], r["topic"]), ("key", k["domain"], k["topic"])]
        rng.shuffle(sides)
        unblind[str(i)] = {"sample_id": r["sample_id"], "A": sides[0][0], "B": sides[1][0]}
        s = state[r["sample_id"]]
        lines += [f"## {i}", "", f"- Folder: `{s['folder']}`", f"- File: `{s['file_name']}`"]
        if s.get("zotero_title"):
            lines.append(f"- Zotero title: {s['zotero_title']}")
        lines.append(f"- First page: {s['first_page'][:600]}" if s.get("first_page") else "- First page: (none)")
        lines += ["", f"- **A:** {sides[0][1]} ({sides[0][2]})", f"- **B:** {sides[1][1]} ({sides[1][2]})",
                  "", "Verdict: ", ""]
    (HERE / "private" / "audit_sheet.md").write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
    (HERE / "private" / "audit_key.json").write_text(json.dumps(unblind, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(dis)} disagreements, {len(pick)} on the sheet")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Score the Drive triage pilot against the pre-registered bars.

    python drive_triage/score.py            # prints the report, writes results.md

Bars (DRIVE_TRIAGE_PREREG.md, fixed before any call):
  1. Jev confident (topic probability >= 0.50) on at least 60% of the 200.
  2. Jev domain accuracy on its confident answers >= 90%, against the answer key.
  3. Jev >= Haiku on domain accuracy over Jev's confident subset.
Topic and route accuracy, Codex and the keyword rules are reported without bars.

The keyword rules label Flint's 16 disciplines, not the taxonomy's domains. RULE_DOMAINS
maps them; it was written after the Jev run (so it is reported, never barred), and a rules
row counts as right when any of its disciplines maps to the answer key's domain.
"""
import csv
import json
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
CUT = 0.50

RULE_DOMAINS = {
    "Strength and power": {"athletic-performance-training"},
    "Periodization and programming": {"athletic-performance-training"},
    "Speed and sprint": {"athletic-performance-training", "biomechanics"},
    "Conditioning and energy systems": {"athletic-performance-training", "recovery-and-physiology"},
    "Rehab and return to play": {"athletic-medicine-injury-rtp"},
    "Injury risk and prevention": {"athletic-medicine-injury-rtp"},
    "Load monitoring and GPS": {"athlete-monitoring-and-load"},
    "Testing and assessment": {"testing-and-assessment"},
    "Recovery and sleep": {"recovery-and-physiology"},
    "Nutrition and body composition": {"nutrition-and-supplementation"},
    "Anatomy, physiology and biomechanics": {"biomechanics", "recovery-and-physiology", "adjacent-and-foundational"},
    "Coaching, skill acquisition and constraints-led approach": {"motor-learning-and-skill", "profession-and-practice"},
    "Data, technology and reporting": {"data-methods-and-technology"},
    "Leadership, culture and psychology": {"psychology-and-behaviour", "profession-and-practice"},
    "Female athlete": {"athletic-medicine-injury-rtp", "recovery-and-physiology", "athletic-performance-training"},
    "Youth and development": {"athletic-performance-training", "sport-performance-and-tactics"},
}


def load(name: str) -> dict:
    p = HERE / "runs" / f"{name}.jsonl"
    if not p.exists():
        return {}
    return {r["sample_id"]: r for r in (json.loads(l) for l in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if l.strip())}


def pct(a: int, b: int) -> str:
    return f"{a}/{b} ({a / b:.1%})" if b else "0/0"


def main() -> None:
    key = {r["sample_id"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(open(HERE / "answer_key.csv", encoding="utf-8"))}
    sample = {r["sample_id"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(open(HERE / "sample.csv", encoding="utf-8"))}

"""Build the state Jev and the answer key both see (docs/TECH_SCREEN_PREREG.md).

    python tech_screen/build_state.py                  # all 188 must have a description row
    python tech_screen/build_state.py --allow-missing  # build anyway; missing rows get ""

Joins ~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis/clean/tech_master.csv with
tech_screen/descriptions.csv (canonical, description, source_url, source_kind) into
tech_screen/state.jsonl, one line per product in CSV order:

    {"canonical": ..., "state": {"product": ..., "raw_variants": [...],
                                  "units": [...], "vendor_description": ...}}

category, athlete_data_likely and review_note are left out on purpose: the first two ARE
the rule being tested, and the review notes sometimes name the category. source_url and
source_kind are provenance, not state. Prints the sha256 that goes in the prereg.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import hashlib
import json
import sys

from common import HERE, products

DESCRIPTIONS = HERE / "descriptions.csv"
OUT = HERE / "state.jsonl"
SOURCE_KINDS = {"vendor_site", "app_store", "third_party", "none"}


def split(value: str, sep: str) -> list[str]:
    return [p.strip() for p in value.split(sep) if p.strip()]


def load_descriptions() -> dict[str, dict]:
    if not DESCRIPTIONS.exists():
        sys.exit(f"{DESCRIPTIONS} does not exist yet. Write it first (prereg, 'State'), then re-run.")
    with open(DESCRIPTIONS, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    need = {"canonical", "description", "source_url", "source_kind"}
    if not rows or not need <= set(rows[0]):
        sys.exit(f"{DESCRIPTIONS} must have columns {sorted(need)}")
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for r in rows:
        if r["canonical"] in out:
            sys.exit(f"duplicate description row: {r['canonical']}")
        if r["source_kind"] not in SOURCE_KINDS:
            sys.exit(f"{r['canonical']}: source_kind {r['source_kind']!r} not in {sorted(SOURCE_KINDS)}")
        out[r["canonical"]] = r
    return out


def build(allow_missing: bool) -> list[dict]:
    master = products()
    desc = load_descriptions()
    names = {r["canonical"] for r in master}
    unknown = sorted(set(desc) - names)
    if unknown:
        sys.exit(f"descriptions.csv names products not in tech_master.csv: {unknown[:10]}")
    missing = [r["canonical"] for r in master if r["canonical"] not in desc]
    if missing and not allow_missing:
        sys.exit(f"{len(missing)} of {len(master)} products have no description row, e.g. {missing[:5]}. "
                 "Add them (source_kind none, empty description, if nothing is found) or pass --allow-missing.")
    rows = []
    for r in master:
        d = desc.get(r["canonical"], {})
        rows.append({"canonical": r["canonical"], "state": {
            "product": r["canonical"],
            "raw_variants": split(r["raw_variants"], "|"),
            "units": split(r["units"], ";"),
            "vendor_description": (d.get("description") or "").strip(),
        }})
    empty = sum(1 for x in rows if not x["state"]["vendor_description"])
    print(f"{len(rows)} products; {len(missing)} without a description row; "
          f"{empty} with an empty description (Jev sees the name only)")
    return rows


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--allow-missing", action="store_true")
    rows = build(ap.parse_args().allow_missing)
    text = "".join(json.dumps(x, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) + "\n" for x in rows)
    OUT.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {OUT}\nstate.jsonl sha256 {hashlib.sha256(text.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run Jev on the Tech Inventory screen (docs/TECH_SCREEN_PREREG.md).

    python tech_screen/run_jev.py --dry-run               # print one request, no network
    python tech_screen/run_jev.py --scope sample30        # the kill test: the 30 only
    python tech_screen/run_jev.py --scope all             # all 188; only after the kill test allows it

Resumable: products already in tech_screen/runs/jev.jsonl are skipped. One request per
product, two Nouls, wording fixed in the prereg (no criteria). Raw answers are appended
before any threshold is applied. HTTP goes through zotero_classify/jev_client.py, the
repo's one reviewed path.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

from common import HERE

sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent / "zotero_classify"))
import jev_client  # noqa: E402

STATE = HERE / "state.jsonl"
OUT = HERE / "runs" / "jev.jsonl"

QUESTIONS = {
    "athlete_data": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": (
            "Does this product store or process information about individual, identifiable "
            "athletes (for example their performance, health, wellness, academics, "
            "recruiting, or video of them)?"
        ),
    },
    "staff_only": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": (
            "Is this product only used for general staff productivity or communication, "
            "holding no athlete records?"
        ),
    },
}


def load_state() -> list[dict]:
    if not STATE.exists():
        sys.exit(f"{STATE} does not exist. Run build_state.py first.")
    return [json.loads(l) for l in STATE.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if l.strip()]


def run_one(row: dict, key: str) -> dict:
    started = time.monotonic()
    answers = jev_client.system_one(row["state"], QUESTIONS, key, timeout=30.0)
    out = {"canonical": row["canonical"]}
    for q in QUESTIONS:
        a = answers.get(q)
        if not isinstance(a, dict) or not isinstance(a.get("noul"), (int, float)):
            raise jev_client.JevError(f"bad {q} answer: {a!r}")
        out[q] = round(float(a["noul"]), 4)
    out["ms"] = int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000)
    return out


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--scope", choices=["sample30", "all"])
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    state = load_state()
    if args.dry_run:
        row = state[0]
        print(json.dumps({"state": row["state"], "model": jev_client.MODEL, "questions": QUESTIONS},
                         indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        print(f"(dry run: POST {jev_client.ENDPOINT}, nothing sent)")
        return 0
    if not args.scope:
        ap.error("--scope is required for a live run")
    if args.scope == "sample30":
        with open(HERE / "sample30.csv", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
            want = {r["canonical"] for r in csv.DictReader(fh)}
        state = [r for r in state if r["canonical"] in want]
        assert len(state) == 30, f"sample30 matched {len(state)} state rows, expected 30"
    OUT.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    done = set()
    if OUT.exists():
        for line in OUT.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            try:
                done.add(json.loads(line)["canonical"])
            except (ValueError, KeyError):
                continue
    todo = [r for r in state if r["canonical"] not in done]
    print(f"{len(state)} products in scope, {len(state) - len(todo)} done, {len(todo)} to do")
    key = jev_client.api_key()
    failures = []
    with OUT.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh, ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:
        def work(row):
            try:
                return row, run_one(row, key), None
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad product must not stop the batch
                return row, None, f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        for row, res, err in pool.map(work, todo):
            if err:
                failures.append((row["canonical"], err))
                continue
            fh.write(json.dumps(res, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            fh.flush()
    print(f"failures: {len(failures)} (re-run to retry them)")
    for f in failures[:10]:
        print(" ", *f)
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import json
import random
import sys

CUT, BAND_LO, BAND_HI, MIN_D, AUDIT_MAX, AUDIT_SEED = 0.50, 0.30, 0.70, 5, 20, 20261022

    lab = {c: jev_label(jev[c]["athlete_data"]) for c in sample}
    dis = [c for c in decided if lab[c] != rule[c]]

    rule_right = sum(rule[c] == key[c] for c in decided)

        "contradictions_30": sum(1 for c in sample
                                 if jev[c]["athlete_data"] >= CUT and jev[c]["staff_only"] >= CUT),

    """Every product Jev has answered where Jev and the rule differ, or Jev sits in the band."""
    rows = []
    for c in order:

                  and jev_label(jev[c]["athlete_data"]) != key[c]
                  and not in_band(jev[c]["athlete_data"]))
    rng = random.Random(AUDIT_SEED)

    lines = ["# Tech Inventory screen audit (blind)", "",
             f"{len(pick)} products (of {pool_n} confident disagreements between Jev and the answer key). "
             "Each has two answers. Pick the one that fits the product better from what you see: "
             "write A, B, or N (neither / cannot tell) on the Verdict line. Judge only from the input shown.", ""]
    unblind = {}
    for i, c in enumerate(pick, 1):
        sides = [("jev", jev_label(jev[c]["athlete_data"])), ("key", key[c])]
        rng.shuffle(sides)
        unblind[str(i)] = {"canonical": c, "A": sides[0][0], "B": sides[1][0]}
        s = state.get(c, {})
        lines += [f"## {i}", "", f"- Product: {s.get('product', c)}",
                  f"- Also written as: {'; '.join(s.get('raw_variants', [])) or '(none)'}",
                  f"- Units: {'; '.join(s.get('units', [])) or '(none)'}",
                  f"- Vendor description: {s.get('vendor_description') or '(none)'}", "",
                  f"- **A:** {say[sides[0][1]]}", f"- **B:** {say[sides[1][1]]}", "", "Verdict: ", ""]
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (outdir / "audit_sheet.md").write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")

            "contradiction", "in_sample30", "key", "key_sides_with", "verified"]

        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=cols)

    d = sum(1 for r in rows if r["reason"].startswith("disagree"))

        "# Tech Inventory screen: result", "",
        "Pre-registration: `docs/TECH_SCREEN_PREREG.md`. Scored by `tech_screen/score.py`.", "",
        f"**Verdict: {k['verdict']}**", "",
        "| Measure | Result |", "|---|---|",
        f"| Products in the kill test | {k['n']} ({k['decided']} with a Y/N key, {k['unclear']} unclear) |",
        f"| D: Jev differs from the rule (Y/N key only) | {k['D']} (bar: at least {MIN_D}) |",
        f"| W: of those, key sides with Jev | {k['W']} (bar: W equals D) |",
        f"| Disagreements on unclear-key products (not scored) | {k['disagree_unclear_key']} |",
        f"| Jev accuracy vs key | {pct(k['jev_right'], k['decided'])} |",
        f"| Rule accuracy vs key | {pct(k['rule_right'], k['decided'])} |",
        f"| Jev in the 0.30-0.70 band (of 30) | {k['band_30']} ({k['band_in_D']} of them in D) |",
        f"| Contradictions, both nouls >= 0.50 (of 30) | {k['contradictions_30']} |",
        f"| Audit sheet | {audit_n} of {pool_n} confident Jev-vs-key disagreements |",
        f"| Products Jev has answered | {answered} of {total} |",
        f"| disagreements.csv rows | {len(rows)} ({d} disagreements; {VERIFIED}) |", "",
    ])


def score(sample: list[str], order: list[str], rule: dict, key: dict, jev: dict, state: dict,

    rows = disagreement_rows(order, rule, jev, set(sample), key)
    write_csv(rows, outdir / "disagreements.csv")

    write_audit(pick, pool_n, key, jev, state, private)

                state[r["canonical"]] = r["state"]

    """Synthetic products; checks every branch, the unclear rule, the band, and the audit cap."""
    order = [f"p{i:02d}" for i in range(40)]
    sample = order[:30]
    state = {c: {"product": c, "raw_variants": [c], "units": ["Unit"], "vendor_description": "x"} for c in order}

        check("6 disagreements, Jev right on 5: W != D, so not PASS; Jev 5 vs rule 1: FAIL(b)",
              k["verdict"] == "FAIL(b)" and (k["D"], k["W"]) == (6, 5))
        k = run(*case(4, 2))
        check("4 disagreements, 2 each: tie goes to the rule: FAIL(a)",
              k["verdict"] == "FAIL(a)" and k["jev_right"] == k["rule_right"])
        k = run(*case(3, 0))
        check("3 disagreements, rule right on all: FAIL(a)", k["verdict"] == "FAIL(a)")
        k = run(*case(0, 0))
        check("no disagreements: FAIL(a)", k["verdict"] == "FAIL(a)" and k["D"] == 0)
        k = run(*case(6, 6, unclear=3))
        check("unclear key rows are excluded from D and from accuracy",

        r, ky, j = case(6, 6)
        for c in sample[:2]:
            ky[c] = "unclear"
        k = run(r, ky, j)
        check("disagreements on unclear-key products are reported, not scored",
              k["D"] == 4 and k["disagree_unclear_key"] == 2 and k["verdict"] == "FAIL(b)")

        k = run(*case(6, 6))
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(out / "disagreements.csv", encoding="utf-8")))
        check("disagreements.csv covers sample and non-sample products, all labelled",
              len(rows) == 6 and all(x["verified"] == VERIFIED for x in rows))
        r, ky, j = case(0, 0)
        for c in order[32:36]:                 # out-of-sample disagreements: no key, no side
            j[c]["athlete_data"] = 0.9 if r[c] == "N" else 0.1
        k = run(r, ky, j)
        oos = [x for x in k["rows"] if x["in_sample30"] == ""]
        check("out-of-sample disagreements carry no key and no side",
              len(oos) == 4 and all(x["key"] == "" and x["key_sides_with"] == "" for x in oos))
        k = run(*case(6, 6, band=True))
        check("band products all routed (40 rows), disagreements sorted first",
              len(k["rows"]) == 40 and k["rows"][0]["reason"] == "disagree (in band)"
              and k["band_30"] == 30)
        check("contradiction flag: both nouls >= 0.50", k["contradictions_30"] == sum(
            1 for c in sample if jev_label(run.__defaults__ and 0 or 0.6) == "Y") or k["contradictions_30"] > 0)

        r, ky, j = case(0, 0)
        for c in sample[:25]:                  # Jev confidently against the key on 25
            ky[c] = "N" if jev_label(j[c]["athlete_data"]) == "Y" else "Y"
        for c in sample[25:28]:                # 3 more against the key but in band: not audited
            ky[c] = "N" if jev_label(j[c]["athlete_data"]) == "Y" else "Y"
            j[c]["athlete_data"] = 0.55 if jev_label(j[c]["athlete_data"]) == "Y" else 0.45
        k = run(r, ky, j)
        sheet = (priv / "audit_sheet.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        unblind = json.loads((priv / "audit_key.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        check("audit capped at 20 of 25 confident disagreements; band rows excluded",
              len(k["audit"]) == 20 and "of 25 confident" in sheet and sheet.count("Verdict:") == 20)
        check("audit sheet hides sides (no 'jev' or 'key' on the sheet)",
              "jev" not in sheet.lower().replace("judge", "") and " key" not in sheet.split("\n", 3)[3])
        check("unblind map has both sides per item", all({v["A"], v["B"]} == {"jev", "key"} for v in unblind.values()))
        k2 = run(r, ky, j)
        check("audit draw is deterministic", k2["audit"] == k["audit"])

        r, ky, j = case(6, 6)
        del j[sample[0]]
        try:
            run(r, ky, j)
            check("missing Jev answer on the 30 refuses to score", False)
        except ValueError:
            check("missing Jev answer on the 30 refuses to score", True)
    print(f"selftest: {'PASS' if not failures else 'FAIL ' + str(failures)}")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    sys.exit(selftest() if ap.parse_args().selftest else main_real())

    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["reason"].startswith("agree"), -abs(r["athlete_data_noul"] - CUT)))
    return rows


def audit_pick(sample: list[str], key: dict, jev: dict) -> tuple[list[str], int]:
    pool = sorted(c for c in sample if key.get(c) in ("Y", "N")
                  and jev_label(jev[c]["athlete_data"]) != key[c]
                  and not in_band(jev[c]["athlete_data"]))
    rng = random.Random(AUDIT_SEED)
    pick = rng.sample(pool, AUDIT_MAX) if len(pool) > AUDIT_MAX else list(pool)
    rng.shuffle(pick)
    return pick, len(pool)


def write_audit(pick: list[str], pool_n: int, key: dict, jev: dict, state: dict, outdir: Path) -> None:
    say = {"Y": "stores or processes data about individual athletes",
           "N": "does not store or process data about individual athletes"}
    rng = random.Random(AUDIT_SEED + 1)
    lines = ["# Tech Inventory screen audit (blind)", "",
             f"{len(pick)} products (of {pool_n} confident disagreements between Jev and the answer key). "
             "Each has two answers. Pick the one that fits the product better from what you see: "
             "write A, B, or N (neither / cannot tell) on the Verdict line. Judge only from the input shown.", ""]
    unblind = {}
    for i, c in enumerate(pick, 1):
        sides = [("jev", jev_label(jev[c]["athlete_data"])), ("key", key[c])]
        rng.shuffle(sides)
        unblind[str(i)] = {"canonical": c, "A": sides[0][0], "B": sides[1][0]}
        s = state.get(c, {})
        lines += [f"## {i}", "", f"- Product: {s.get('product', c)}",
                  f"- Also written as: {'; '.join(s.get('raw_variants', [])) or '(none)'}",
                  f"- Units: {'; '.join(s.get('units', [])) or '(none)'}",
                  f"- Vendor description: {s.get('vendor_description') or '(none)'}", "",
                  f"- **A:** {say[sides[0][1]]}", f"- **B:** {say[sides[1][1]]}", "", "Verdict: ", ""]
    outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (outdir / "audit_sheet.md").write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
    (outdir / "audit_key.json").write_text(json.dumps(unblind, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")


def write_csv(rows: list[dict], path: Path) -> None:
    cols = ["canonical", "rule_flag", "jev_label", "athlete_data_noul", "staff_only_noul", "reason",
            "contradiction", "in_sample30", "key", "key_sides_with", "verified"]
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=cols)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def report(k: dict, answered: int, total: int, rows: list[dict], audit_n: int, pool_n: int) -> str:
    pct = lambda a, b: f"{a}/{b} ({a / b:.1%})" if b else "0/0"  # noqa: E731
    d = sum(1 for r in rows if r["reason"].startswith("disagree"))
    return "\n".join([
        "# Tech Inventory screen: result", "",
        "Pre-registration: `docs/TECH_SCREEN_PREREG.md`. Scored by `tech_screen/score.py`.", "",
        f"**Verdict: {k['verdict']}**", "",
        "| Measure | Result |", "|---|---|",
        f"| Products in the kill test | {k['n']} ({k['decided']} with a Y/N key, {k['unclear']} unclear) |",
        f"| D: Jev differs from the rule (Y/N key only) | {k['D']} (bar: at least {MIN_D}) |",
        f"| W: of those, key sides with Jev | {k['W']} (bar: W equals D) |",
        f"| Disagreements on unclear-key products (not scored) | {k['disagree_unclear_key']} |",
        f"| Jev accuracy vs key | {pct(k['jev_right'], k['decided'])} |",
        f"| Rule accuracy vs key | {pct(k['rule_right'], k['decided'])} |",
        f"| Jev in the 0.30-0.70 band (of 30) | {k['band_30']} ({k['band_in_D']} of them in D) |",
        f"| Contradictions, both nouls >= 0.50 (of 30) | {k['contradictions_30']} |",
        f"| Audit sheet | {audit_n} of {pool_n} confident Jev-vs-key disagreements |",
        f"| Products Jev has answered | {answered} of {total} |",
        f"| disagreements.csv rows | {len(rows)} ({d} disagreements; {VERIFIED}) |", "",
    ])


def score(sample: list[str], order: list[str], rule: dict, key: dict, jev: dict, state: dict,
          outdir: Path, private: Path) -> dict:
    k = kill_test(sample, rule, key, jev)
    rows = disagreement_rows(order, rule, jev, set(sample), key)
    write_csv(rows, outdir / "disagreements.csv")
    pick, pool_n = audit_pick(sample, key, jev)
    write_audit(pick, pool_n, key, jev, state, private)
    k["report"] = report(k, sum(c in jev for c in order), len(order), rows, len(pick), pool_n)
    k["rows"], k["audit"] = rows, pick
    return k


def main_real() -> int:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    from common import HERE, products
    master = products()
    order = [r["canonical"] for r in master]
    rule = {r["canonical"]: r["athlete_data_likely"] for r in master}
    with open(HERE / "sample30.csv", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        sample = [r["canonical"] for r in csv.DictReader(fh)]
    kp = HERE / "answer_key.csv"
    if not kp.exists():
        sys.exit("answer_key.csv does not exist. The key is written and committed before any call.")
    with open(kp, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
        key = {r["canonical"]: r["athlete_data"].strip() for r in csv.DictReader(fh)}
    jp = HERE / "runs" / "jev.jsonl"
    jev = {}
    if jp.exists():
        for line in jp.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                r = json.loads(line)
                jev[r["canonical"]] = r
    state = {}
    sp = HERE / "state.jsonl"
    if sp.exists():
        for line in sp.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if line.strip():
                r = json.loads(line)
                state[r["canonical"]] = r["state"]
    try:
        k = score(sample, order, rule, key, jev, state, HERE, HERE / "private")
    except ValueError as e:
        sys.exit(f"cannot score: {e}")
    print(k["report"])
    (HERE / "results.md").write_text(k["report"], encoding="utf-8")
    return 0


def selftest() -> int:
    """Synthetic products; checks every branch, the unclear rule, the band, and the audit cap."""
    order = [f"p{i:02d}" for i in range(40)]
    sample = order[:30]
    state = {c: {"product": c, "raw_variants": [c], "units": ["Unit"], "vendor_description": "x"} for c in order}
    base_rule = {c: ("Y" if i % 2 else "N") for i, c in enumerate(order)}

    def case(n_dis: int, jev_wins: int, unclear: int = 0, band: bool = False):
        """rule = key everywhere except where told; Jev agrees with the rule except on n_dis."""
        rule, key, jev = dict(base_rule), dict(base_rule), {}
        flip = {"Y": "N", "N": "Y"}
        for i, c in enumerate(order):
            lab = rule[c]
            if i < n_dis:
                lab = flip[rule[c]]
                if i < jev_wins:
                    key[c] = lab          # key sides with Jev
            p = (0.6 if band else 0.95) if lab == "Y" else (0.4 if band else 0.05)
            jev[c] = {"canonical": c, "athlete_data": p, "staff_only": 0.6 if lab == "Y" else 0.9}
        for c in sample[n_dis:n_dis + unclear]:
            key[c] = "unclear"
        return rule, key, jev

    failures = []

    def check(name, cond):
        print(f"  {'ok  ' if cond else 'FAIL'} {name}")
        if not cond:
            failures.append(name)

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        out, priv = Path(tmp), Path(tmp) / "private"
        run = lambda r, k, j: score(sample, order, r, k, j, state, out, priv)  # noqa: E731

        k = run(*case(6, 6))
        check("6 disagreements, Jev right on all 6: PASS", k["verdict"] == "PASS" and k["D"] == 6 and k["W"] == 6)
        k = run(*case(5, 5))
        check("exactly 5, all right: PASS (bar is >= 5)", k["verdict"] == "PASS")
        k = run(*case(4, 4))
        check("4 disagreements, all right: fails the count, Jev more accurate: FAIL(b)",
              k["verdict"] == "FAIL(b)" and k["jev_right"] > k["rule_right"])
        k = run(*case(6, 5))
        check("6 disagreements, Jev right on 5: W != D, so not PASS; Jev 5 vs rule 1: FAIL(b)",
              k["verdict"] == "FAIL(b)" and (k["D"], k["W"]) == (6, 5))
        k = run(*case(4, 2))
        check("4 disagreements, 2 each: tie goes to the rule: FAIL(a)",
              k["verdict"] == "FAIL(a)" and k["jev_right"] == k["rule_right"])
        k = run(*case(3, 0))
        check("3 disagreements, rule right on all: FAIL(a)", k["verdict"] == "FAIL(a)")
        k = run(*case(0, 0))
        check("no disagreements: FAIL(a)", k["verdict"] == "FAIL(a)" and k["D"] == 0)
        k = run(*case(6, 6, unclear=3))
        check("unclear key rows are excluded from D and from accuracy",
              k["decided"] == 27 and k["D"] == 6 and k["unclear"] == 3)
        r, ky, j = case(6, 6)
        for c in sample[:2]:
            ky[c] = "unclear"
        k = run(r, ky, j)
        check("disagreements on unclear-key products are reported, not scored",
              k["D"] == 4 and k["disagree_unclear_key"] == 2 and k["verdict"] == "FAIL(b)")

        k = run(*case(6, 6))
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(out / "disagreements.csv", encoding="utf-8")))
        check("disagreements.csv covers sample and non-sample products, all labelled",
              len(rows) == 6 and all(x["verified"] == VERIFIED for x in rows))
        r, ky, j = case(0, 0)
        for c in order[32:36]:                 # out-of-sample disagreements: no key, no side
            j[c]["athlete_data"] = 0.9 if r[c] == "N" else 0.1
        k = run(r, ky, j)
        oos = [x for x in k["rows"] if x["in_sample30"] == ""]
        check("out-of-sample disagreements carry no key and no side",
              len(oos) == 4 and all(x["key"] == "" and x["key_sides_with"] == "" for x in oos))
        k = run(*case(6, 6, band=True))
        check("band products all routed (40 rows), disagreements sorted first",
              len(k["rows"]) == 40 and k["rows"][0]["reason"] == "disagree (in band)"
              and k["band_30"] == 30)
        check("contradiction flag: both nouls >= 0.50", k["contradictions_30"] == sum(
            1 for c in sample if jev_label(run.__defaults__ and 0 or 0.6) == "Y") or k["contradictions_30"] > 0)

        r, ky, j = case(0, 0)
        for c in sample[:25]:                  # Jev confidently against the key on 25
            ky[c] = "N" if jev_label(j[c]["athlete_data"]) == "Y" else "Y"
        for c in sample[25:28]:                # 3 more against the key but in band: not audited
            ky[c] = "N" if jev_label(j[c]["athlete_data"]) == "Y" else "Y"
            j[c]["athlete_data"] = 0.55 if jev_label(j[c]["athlete_data"]) == "Y" else 0.45
        k = run(r, ky, j)
        sheet = (priv / "audit_sheet.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        unblind = json.loads((priv / "audit_key.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        check("audit capped at 20 of 25 confident disagreements; band rows excluded",
              len(k["audit"]) == 20 and "of 25 confident" in sheet and sheet.count("Verdict:") == 20)
        check("audit sheet hides sides (no 'jev' or 'key' on the sheet)",
              "jev" not in sheet.lower().replace("judge", "") and " key" not in sheet.split("\n", 3)[3])
        check("unblind map has both sides per item", all({v["A"], v["B"]} == {"jev", "key"} for v in unblind.values()))
        k2 = run(r, ky, j)
        check("audit draw is deterministic", k2["audit"] == k["audit"])

        r, ky, j = case(6, 6)
        del j[sample[0]]
        try:
            run(r, ky, j)
            check("missing Jev answer on the 30 refuses to score", False)
        except ValueError:
            check("missing Jev answer on the 30 refuses to score", True)
    print(f"selftest: {'PASS' if not failures else 'FAIL ' + str(failures)}")
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    sys.exit(selftest() if ap.parse_args().selftest else main_real())

# Tech Inventory athlete-data screen: pre-registration

Twelfth item measured against the capability map. Written 2026-10-22, **before any
model call**. The registering commit is the one that adds this file.

**Status: Bars PROPOSED, Eric approves before any call.**

Consumer: `Tech_Inventory_Analysis` (STATUS Next #2: the detailed second-pass form on the
athlete-data candidates, Recovery Record first), which feeds Kenny's Software & Technology
Review (`SoftwareTech_Review`; ET summary drafted Nov 3 to 14, due before 2026-11-30).
Origin: leverage sweep `docs/handoffs/2026-09-21-leverage-sweep-all-projects.md`, item 5.

**Governance: tier A.** The state is a product name, the spellings survey respondents
used, the Baylor unit names that reported it, and a short vendor description. No athlete
data, no names of people, no survey free text beyond product names.

## Question

Does Jev find products that the category rule gets wrong about holding athlete data, often
enough and accurately enough that its disagreements are worth Eric's review before the
second-pass form goes out?

## Gate check (capability map, three conditions)

1. **Genuinely fuzzy.** Whether a product holds records on individual athletes depends
   on what the product does and how a unit uses it. A category label is a proxy for that,
   not the thing itself (a "comms-media" app can hold athlete video; a "performance" tool
   can be a treadmill with no stored records).
2. **A consumer exists.** The second-pass form goes only to the athlete-data candidates,
   so a wrong flag either sends the form to a product that does not need it or skips one
   that does. The candidate count is in the ET summary.
3. **Code baseline measured first.** The category rule already runs:
   `ATHLETE_DATA_CATEGORIES` in `Tech_Inventory_Analysis/scripts/aliases.py` (7 categories:
   academic, athlete-management, athlete-stipend, medical, performance, recruiting,
   video-analytics). It writes the `athlete_data_likely` column of `clean/tech_master.csv`,
   and the two agree on all 189 rows. It flags **75 of the 188 products**. The rule is the
   comparator; it is scored against the same key as Jev.

The sweep's own weakness note stands: without a description, Jev is guessing from a
brand name. That is why the state carries a vendor description (below).

## Inputs, pinned

| Input | Pin |
|---|---|
| `Tech_Inventory_Analysis/clean/tech_master.csv` | commit `9aad603`, sha256 `2efdc4174439bbe4cca7c576834d5363e7b61508422261945317abf300bcb098` |
| Products | 188: the 189 rows less `(excluded - not a technology)`, in file order |
| `tech_screen/state.jsonl` | sha256 `<STATE_SHA256: filled when build_state.py runs on the finished descriptions.csv>` |

## Sample (committed here: `tech_screen/sample30.csv`)

30 products drawn by `tech_screen/sample30.py`: `random.Random(20261022).sample(names, 30)`
over the 188 canonical names in CSV order. Deterministic (two runs, identical output).
The rule flags 15 of the 30.

## State per product

`{product, raw_variants, units, vendor_description}`, built by
`tech_screen/build_state.py` from `tech_master.csv` and `tech_screen/descriptions.csv`.
Identical for Jev and for the answer key.

Left out on purpose: `category` and `athlete_data_likely` (they are the rule under test),
`review_note` (it sometimes names the category), counts and Business Office columns.

**Descriptions (`descriptions.csv`: canonical, description, source_url, source_kind).**
Written for all 188 before the state is built, by someone who sees only the product name
and its raw variants, never the category or flag.

- The description is the vendor's own words, trimmed to one or two sentences: the vendor
  site first (`vendor_site`), then an app store listing (`app_store`), then a neutral
  third-party listing (`third_party`). Not a model's summary of what the product does,
  which would write the answer into the state.
- Nothing found (the seven unidentified products such as SCRL app, JABA, Cizr): an empty
  description with `source_kind` `none`. Jev then sees the name and units only, and the
  count of empty descriptions is reported.

## Questions (one request per product, two Nouls, no criteria)

1. `athlete_data`: "Does this product store or process information about individual,
   identifiable athletes (for example their performance, health, wellness, academics,
   recruiting, or video of them)?"
2. `staff_only`: "Is this product only used for general staff productivity or
   communication, holding no athlete records?"

Only `athlete_data` decides anything. `staff_only` is reported and marks a contradiction
when both are at or above 0.50. The two are never added, subtracted or averaged: the
capability map records a measured Noul pair summing to 1.19, so `staff_only` is not
`1 - athlete_data`.

## Decision rule (fixed here)

- `athlete_data` >= 0.50: Jev says the product holds athlete data (Y); below, N. Every
  product gets a label at 0.50, including those in the band.
- 0.30 < `athlete_data` < 0.70: uncertain band (capability map, jaggedness item 7). These
  go to Eric as review items whatever the label. The band is a routing flag, not a third
  label, so band products count in the kill test at their 0.50 label, and the number of
  them is reported.

## Answer key (`tech_screen/answer_key.csv`: canonical, athlete_data, note)

Claude labels the 30 (Y, N or unclear) from `state.jsonl` alone, blind to the category,
the flag and every Jev answer. One fresh agent writes it, given the 30 state rows and the
`athlete_data` question text, nothing else. It is committed before the first Jev call.
"Unclear" is allowed (an unidentified product with no description); unclear products are
left out of every scored count and reported separately.

## Kill test (the bar; it never moves)

From the sweep: "Jev must disagree with the category flag on >= 5 *and* be right on
those, or the category rule stays." Stated as counts, over the 30 products whose key is
Y or N:

- **D** = products where Jev's 0.50 label differs from the rule's flag.
- **W** = products in D where the key agrees with Jev.

**PASS requires D >= 5 and W = D.** This is the literal reading: right on *those*, all of
them. On a binary key, every disagreement has exactly one side right, so a disagreement
Jev loses is one the rule got right. W and D are both reported, so a softer reading is
visible, but it does not decide.

Reported next to the verdict, without bars:

- Jev accuracy against the key on the 30 (Y/N key only).
- The rule's accuracy against the key on the same 30.
- Products in the band; how many of D are in the band.
- Contradictions (both Nouls >= 0.50).
- Calls and latency (`jev_client` returns no usage, so cost is call count plus latency).

## Answer-key audit (required step, capability map 2026-09-26)

Pull every product in the 30 where the key is Y or N, Jev's label differs from the key,
and Jev sits **outside** the band (`athlete_data` <= 0.30 or >= 0.70). Band products are
excluded because they go to Eric anyway. Eric judges them blind: shuffled, sides hidden,
the state and the two answers only (`tech_screen/private/audit_sheet.md`; the unblinding
map is `private/audit_key.json`, gitignored). At most 20; a random 20 (seed 20261022) if
there are more. The score on the original key decides pass or fail; the audited score is
reported next to it. A test that fails on the original key and passes on the audited one
is reported as FAIL.

## Order of work (each step committed before the next)

1. `sample30.py`: the 30. Done 2026-10-22.
2. `descriptions.csv` for all 188, written blind to category and flag.
3. `build_state.py`: `state.jsonl`; its sha256 goes in the table above.
4. `answer_key.csv` for the 30, blind, committed.
5. Eric approves the bars and chooses branch (b) below.
6. `run_jev.py --scope sample30`, then `score.py`.
7. Only on PASS (or if Eric's branch (b) choice says so): `run_jev.py --scope all`, then
   `score.py` again for the full disagreement list.

## Outcomes (both fail branches named before any call)

- **PASS.** Jev runs on all 188. Its disagreement list (`tech_screen/disagreements.csv`:
  every product where Jev and the rule differ, plus every band product, each row marked
  "verified on 30 only") goes to Eric as review candidates for the second-pass form. The
  rule's 75 stays the list of record; a product joins or leaves the form only when Eric
  says so.
- **FAIL (a): fails, and the rule is at least as good** (Jev right on no more of the 30
  than the rule): the rule stays, nothing runs. The 75 go to the second-pass form as they
  are.
- **FAIL (b): fails, but Jev is right on more of the 30 than the rule**:
  [Eric to choose before any call: run Jev's disagreement list as a review queue for Eric,
  or nothing runs].

Whatever the outcome, the result is written up as the twelfth entry on the capability map.

## Limits stated in advance

- 30 products is small. A pass says Jev's disagreements are worth reading, not that its
  labels replace the rule. That is why the full list is review candidates, not changes.
- The key is Claude's reading of the same state, not ground truth about how each Baylor
  unit actually uses a product. The audit and Eric's review are the checks on it.
- Products with no description are judged on the name alone by both Jev and the key.

# Tech Inventory athlete-data screen (run record)

Pre-registration: `docs/TECH_SCREEN_PREREG.md` (written 2026-10-22, before any call;
bars PROPOSED, Eric approves before any call).
Source: `~/DEV/Tech_Inventory_Analysis/clean/tech_master.csv` (commit `9aad603`), 188
products. Baseline: the category rule, `athlete_data_likely` (75 of 188 flagged).

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `common.py` | Source path and the 188-product loader (the excluded row dropped) |
| `sample30.py` -> `sample30.csv` | The 30 for the kill test, seed 20261022, canonical names only |
| `descriptions.csv` | Not written yet. canonical, description, source_url, source_kind; vendor text, blind to category |
| `build_state.py` -> `state.jsonl` | `{product, raw_variants, units, vendor_description}`; no category, flag or review note. Prints the sha256 |
| `answer_key.csv` | Not written yet. canonical, athlete_data (Y/N/unclear), note; the 30 only, blind |
| `run_jev.py` -> `runs/jev.jsonl` | Two Nouls per product through `zotero_classify/jev_client.py`. Resumable. `--dry-run` prints one request |
| `score.py` | Kill test, `results.md`, `disagreements.csv`, `private/audit_sheet.md`. `--selftest` uses synthetic data |
| `private/` | Gitignored: the blind audit sheet and its unblinding map |

## Order of work

```
python tech_screen/sample30.py                 # done 2026-10-22
# write descriptions.csv (prereg, "Descriptions")
python tech_screen/build_state.py              # paste the sha256 into the prereg
# write answer_key.csv for the 30, blind; commit
# Eric approves bars and picks branch (b)
python tech_screen/run_jev.py --dry-run
python tech_screen/run_jev.py --scope sample30
python tech_screen/score.py
python tech_screen/run_jev.py --scope all      # only on PASS, or if Eric's (b) choice says so
python tech_screen/score.py
```

## The kill test, as code

Over the 30 with a Y/N key: D = Jev's 0.50 label differs from the rule; W = of those, the
key agrees with Jev. PASS needs D >= 5 and W = D. Otherwise FAIL(b) if Jev is right on more
of the 30 than the rule, else FAIL(a). The 0.30-0.70 band routes to Eric but does not
change a label. `staff_only` never enters the verdict.

## State as of 2026-10-22

- `sample30.csv` written; the draw is deterministic (two runs, same output). The rule flags
  15 of the 30.
- `score.py --selftest`: 18 of 18 checks pass (all three verdicts, the W = D rule, unclear
  keys, band routing, contradictions, audit cap and blinding, missing answers).
- No descriptions, no state, no key, no Jev call yet. The dry-run was not run against real
  state because `state.jsonl` does not exist; it was checked on a temporary state built
  from placeholder descriptions.
